title: Endovascular and open surgical repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysms: outcomes, treatment trends, and risk factors for mortality in an 18-year monocentric study
summary:
Since 1991, the so-called EVAR - an endovascular treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysms - has been available. This method is particularly suitable for patients who have many concomitant diseases and would have an increased mortality risk with an open surgical repair (OSR).
Thanks to technical advances, EVAR has been continuously developed over the last 30 years - with smaller procedures, fewer complications and shorter hospital stays.
Studies show that EVAR offers better survival rates than open surgery in the first 30 days after the procedure. In the long term, however, the advantage is offset and EVAR patients require more frequent follow-up treatment. EVAR is therefore only recommended if the vascular anatomy is suitable. Open surgery is often better for younger, healthy patients.
In recent decades, the use of EVAR has increased overall, regardless of patient age.
This study examines the outcomes, risk factors and treatment trends associated with EVAR and OSR in a vascular center over the age of 18.
conditions: Abdominal aortic aneurysm, without mention of rupture

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients with AAA (infrarenal or juxtarenal) who underwent endovascular or open surgery in our clinic between 01.01.2005 and 31.12.2022 will be included in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
• Penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU)
• Pararenal aortic aneurysm
• Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm
• Mycotic aortic aneurysm
• Infectious aortic aneurysm
• Ruptured aortic aneurysm
